subject: Restore drill window + Redwood support coverage (Northbridge) — Dec 17
body:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@northbridgehealth.org>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@northbridgehealth.org>, IT Ops On-Call <it-oncall@northbridgehealth.org>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 9, 2025 at 4:12 PM PT
Subject: Restore drill window + Redwood support coverage (Northbridge) — Dec 17

Jordan — confirming we have Redwood coverage for the Dec 17 restore drill window.

Proposed drill window (per our last call):
- Wed Dec 17, 09:00–13:00 PT (primary)
- Backup window in case of slip: 13:00–15:00 PT

Redwood coverage plan:
- Primary (Solutions): Markus Klein (me) — live on the bridge for the full window
- Secondary (AE): Ava Chen — available for coordination/escalations + comms
- Security escalation: Aisha Rahman — on standby for key/KMS/HSM questions or audit/evidence needs

We’ll run the “restore to new cluster” flow and do a cutover at the end (pending validation gates).

Escalation path during the drill:
1) Start with me in-thread / on bridge
2) If we hit an infra/tooling issue that blocks restore steps, I’ll pull in Redwood SRE via our internal on-call (you don’t need to page them)
3) If we hit a security controls question (KMS, key rotation, logging redaction), I’ll loop Aisha

Contingencies we’re planning for (so we can pre-approve actions):
- Object storage permissions (AccessDenied) on the backup repo (S3/minio) — validate IAM policy + bucket policy before start
- KMS key policy / cross-account usage — confirm which role performs decrypt + list/get
- Restore running long (maintenance window risk) — decision point at T+2h for “continue vs pause and re-scope”
- Backup artifact integrity (checksum mismatch / partial upload) — use verify step and re-stage if needed
- Postgres restore/PITR WAL coverage gaps — confirm WAL archiving and PITR target timestamp policy
- Maintenance mode toggling / write-path blocking — confirm application owners are aware and have comms ready

Next steps:
- Jordan: can you confirm the bridge link + who from Northbridge will be hands-on keyboard vs observer?
- Priya: please share which storage backend you’re using for the drill (S3 w/ VPC endpoint vs on-prem minio) and the region

Attaching the checklist we’ll follow on our side (PDF). If you’d like, we can also provide a run-of-show doc for roles and timestamps.

Thanks,
Markus

—
Markus Klein
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, Dec 9, 2025 at 5:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Restore drill window + Redwood support coverage (Northbridge) — Dec 17

Jordan — adding Aisha Rahman (Redwood) as the security/KMS escalation for the drill.

(a) KMS policy questions:
- Aisha can join live if we hit policy/role assumptions, key policy conditions, or evidence/logging concerns.
- For “what exact permissions does the restore role need?” we have a least-privilege template we can sanity-check against.

(b) Time-box guidance (based on prior drills):
- T+60 min: restore should be “making forward progress” (DB restore underway or completed; artifacts downloading)
- T+120 min: decision point — if still blocked on permissions/networking, recommend pausing and switching to “preflight fix” mode rather than burning the remaining window
- T+150 min: last call to do cutover steps (DNS/TLS/etc.). If we’re not ready, we stop and document findings.

We’ll also run explicit validation gates before cutover:
- API health checks
- a minimal smoke test suite
- confirm maintenance mode off and write paths unblocked

Aisha — anything else you want Northbridge to have ready for the KMS part?

Markus


From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Matthews <jordan.matthews@northbridgehealth.org>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@northbridgehealth.org>, IT Ops On-Call <it-oncall@northbridgehealth.org>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Dec 9, 2025 at 6:01 PM PT
Subject: Re: Restore drill window + Redwood support coverage (Northbridge) — Dec 17

Jordan / Priya — for the SSE-KMS portion, the most common gotcha is the S3 access role can List/Get but cannot use the CMK due to key policy conditions.

To make the drill smooth, please have ready:
- The IAM role ARN that will execute restore (and any role it assumes)
- The KMS key ARN used for the backup bucket
- The key policy statement(s) that grant kms:Decrypt / kms:GenerateDataKey to the restore role
- Whether you require encryption context conditions (e.g., aws:s3:arn)

We can do a 10-minute preflight on Dec 16 (any time) to validate the policy shape before the drill.

Also confirming: Redwood does not need access to plaintext keys. We only require that the role you run the toolkit under can call KMS as permitted by your policies.

Aisha

Aisha Rahman
Security, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Restore drill window + Redwood support coverage (Northbridge) — Dec 17

All — summarizing the plan + concrete contingencies so we’re aligned.

DR drill schedule
- Dec 16 10:30–10:45 PT: KMS/S3 preflight (Priya + Aisha + Markus)
- Dec 17 08:50 PT: join bridge, confirm comms + decision-maker
- Dec 17 09:00–13:00 PT: restore drill (restore-to-new-cluster + validation + optional cutover)

Decision points / stop criteria
- T+120 min: if blocked on permissions/networking, pause the drill and switch to documenting remediation steps (don’t burn the whole window)
- T+150 min: if validation gates are not passing, do NOT cut over

Concrete contingencies & what we’ll do
1) AccessDenied on S3 (List/Get/Put)
   - Confirm role session name + assumed-role chain
   - Validate bucket policy principal matches assumed role ARN

2) KMS decrypt failures
   - Check key policy allows the restore role + correct conditions (encryption context)
   - If key policy fix required, Jordan/Priya to apply (Redwood will not edit customer IAM)

3) Restore artifact download stalls / throttling
   - Temporarily raise S3 request limits / adjust concurrency
   - If still stalled, re-run with lower parallelism to complete within window

4) DB restore conflicts / locks
   - Ensure maintenance mode is enabled before DB restore
   - If DB restore doesn’t progress, stop and capture logs + state

5) Cert/DNS cutover blocked
   - Validate using cluster-local endpoint first
   - If cert issuance is a dependency, keep cutover optional and treat as stretch goal

6) Toolkit command confusion
   - We’ll use the Redwood operator checklist and post each command in the bridge chat before running

I’m sharing a run-of-show doc (link) with roles/timestamps. If you want edits, comment inline.

Doc: Northbridge_DR_Restore_Drill_RunOfShow_v3.docx (Google Doc link)

Markus

For Dec 17 decision-maker: that’ll be me.

One more contingency: if the restore exceeds the maintenance window, we need a clear message for app teams about expected 503s / write rejection. Can you provide a short blurb we can paste into our incident channel?

Jordan


From: Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@northbridgehealth.org>, IT Ops On-Call <it-oncall@northbridgehealth.org>, Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Dec 11, 2025 at 10:46 AM PT
Subject: Re: Restore drill window + Redwood support coverage (Northbridge) — Dec 17

Yes — here’s a paste-ready blurb.

---
Status: Planned maintenance (DR restore drill)
Impact: During the restore window, Redwood Private control plane APIs will reject write operations (expected 503/409 with actionable error message) while the system is in maintenance mode. Read-only operations may be degraded.
What to do: Do not retry write-heavy workflows; pause job runners and queue writes until we announce maintenance mode is lifted.
Next update: We’ll post an update every 30 minutes, or immediately if we hit a blocker that changes the timeline.
---

If you want, we can tailor the exact status code/message to what your app teams see (depends on your integration paths). We’ll confirm in the drill once maintenance mode is toggled.

Markus
